items.title: Air Canada halts Cuba flights as fuel crisis deepens

featured_image.name: Air Canada suspends flights to Cuba because of aviation fuel shortage

items.description:
Cuba enacted drastic emergency measures on Monday as the island nation grapples with a rapidly worsening energy crisis exacerbated by U.S. pressure to cut off its oil supply. The government has mandated a four-day workweek for state-owned companies, reduced school hours, suspended university classes, and slashed public transportation services while restricting fuel sales.[1][2][3][4]

The emergency protocols took effect as Havana's streets fell notably silent, with the communist government scrambling to preserve rapidly depleting fuel reserves. Air Canada announced Monday it is suspending all flights to Cuba after Cuban authorities warned that aviation fuel would no longer be available at the island's airports beginning Tuesday, February 10.[5][6][4]

items.title: Israel warns US it may strike Iran alone over missile threat

featured_image.name: Netanyahu to meet Trump in Washington Wednesday to discuss ...

items.description:
Israeli defense officials have told their American counterparts that Jerusalem is prepared to launch unilateral military strikes against Iran's ballistic missile infrastructure if Tehran crosses what Israel considers a critical security threshold, according to multiple reports citing security sources.

"We told the Americans we will strike alone if Iran crosses the red line we set on ballistic missiles," a senior Israeli source told The Jerusalem Post, adding that Israel has not yet reached that threshold but is continuously monitoring developments inside Iran. The officials described Iran's expanding missile capabilities as an existential threat and outlined operational plans to dismantle key manufacturing sites and production facilities.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Alphabet raises $20B in bond sale amid record AI-driven demand

featured_image.name: 2+ Hundred Alphabet Inc Headquarters Royalty-Free Images ...

items.description:
Alphabet, the parent company of Google, sold $20 billion in bonds on Monday in a deal that attracted more than $100 billion in investor orders, underscoring the enormous appetite for debt tied to the artificial intelligence boom.[1][2]

The seven-part offering of senior unsecured notes exceeded the company's initial expectations of $15 billion, with demand described by Bloomberg as among the strongest ever for a corporate bond offering. Alphabet is also planning an additional sterling bond sale that may include a rare 100-year "century bond," which would mark the first such long-dated debt issued by a technology company since the dot-com era.[3][4][5][1]

items.title: Cuba halts airline refueling for a month amid energy crisis

featured_image.name: Airlines will no longer be able to refuel on Cuba as U.S. blockade ...

items.description:
Cuba has notified international carriers that aviation fuel will be unavailable across the island's airports for an entire month, forcing major airlines to suspend or reroute flights as the nation's energy crisis reaches a critical stage.

The Cuban government issued an official Notice to Air Missions (NOTAM) on Sunday evening warning that Jet A-1 fuel will not be available from February 10 through March 11 at all nine international airports, including Havana's José Martí International Airport, Varadero, Santa Clara, Holguín, Santiago de Cuba, and Cayo Coco. The measure is expected to disrupt more than 400 scheduled weekly flights.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Bennu asteroid samples challenge theory on how life's building blocks formed

featured_image.name: Life's ingredients have been found in samples from asteroid ...

items.description:
Amino acids, the molecular building blocks essential for life, may have formed in icy, radiation-rich conditions at the edge of the early solar system rather than in warm water, according to new research published today in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. The findings, based on analysis of samples from asteroid Bennu returned to Earth by NASA's OSIRIS-REx mission in 2023, challenge decades of assumptions about how life's basic ingredients first arose.

"Our results flip the script on how we have typically thought amino acids formed in asteroids," said Allison Baczynski, assistant research professor of geosciences at Penn State and co-lead author of the study. "It now looks like there are many conditions where these building blocks of life can form, not just when there's warm liquid water."[1][2]

items.title: Mexico suspends oil shipments to Cuba to avoid US tariffs

featured_image.name: Mexico to send oil to Cuba despite Trump pressure - Bloomberg

items.description:
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum confirmed on Monday that Mexico has suspended oil shipments to Cuba to avoid tariffs threatened by the Trump administration, calling the US sanctions "very unfair" as she warned that the measures would "strangle" the crisis-stricken island nation.

"This sanction being imposed on countries that sell oil to Cuba is very unfair... sanctions that harm the people are not right," Sheinbaum told reporters at her daily press briefing. "You cannot strangle a people like this—it's very unfair, very unfair."[1]

items.title: US, Bangladesh sign trade deal cutting tariffs to 19%

featured_image.name: US strikes new deal with Bangladesh to trim tariff rate on ...

items.description: The United States and Bangladesh have signed a trade agreement reducing US tariffs on Bangladeshi goods to 19 percent and establishing a mechanism for duty-free treatment of certain apparel products made with American materials. The deal, finalized Monday, comes just days before Bangladesh holds its first general election since the ouster of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in 2024.

items.title: Trump to visit China in April for Xi summit

featured_image.name: Trump, Xi discuss Taiwan and soybeans in call aimed at easing China, US relations

items.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump will travel to Beijing during the first week of April for a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, according to a Politico report citing three people familiar with the plans. The trip would mark the first visit by a sitting American president to China since Trump's own 2017 state visit during his first term.[1][2]

The visit comes as the world's two largest economies seek to stabilize relations following months of trade tensions, including an $11 billion U.S. arms deal with Taiwan and Chinese military exercises surrounding the island. Trump has described the upcoming trip as a "business trip" aimed at securing further trade wins.[3][2]

items.title: Eight Muslim nations condemn Israel's West Bank annexation moves

featured_image.name: Israel approves biggest expansion of West Bank settlements ...

items.description:
Eight predominantly Muslim countries issued a joint statement on Monday condemning Israel's newly approved measures in the occupied West Bank, calling them illegal annexation attempts that violate international law and threaten regional stability.

The foreign ministers of Turkey, Egypt, Jordan, Indonesia, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates denounced Israel's Sunday decision as an effort to impose "unlawful Israeli sovereignty, entrenching settlement activity, and enforcing a new legal and administrative reality in the occupied West Bank, thereby accelerating attempts at its illegal annexation and the displacement of the Palestinian people."[1][2]

The joint statement, posted on the Turkish Foreign Ministry's website, emphasized that "Israel has no sovereignty over the occupied Palestinian territory" and warned that such actions "fuel violence and conflict in the region."[1]

items.title: Ukraine exposes 21 Russian drone makers, says most unsanctioned

featured_image.name: Ukrainian intelligence agency exposes 21 Russian companies ...

items.description:
Ukraine's Main Intelligence Directorate (HUR) has published new data identifying 21 Russian companies involved in developing and producing drones for Russia's war against Ukraine, with officials highlighting that more than half of the listed firms remain free from international sanctions.

The data, released on the HUR's War & Sanctions portal, names manufacturers responsible for producing a range of unmanned aerial vehicles currently deployed against Ukrainian forces and civilians, including cargo drones, first-person-view (FPV) attack drones, and AI-enabled kamikaze systems.[1]

items.title: Uber to buy Turkish delivery startup Getir for $435 million

featured_image.name: Uber seeks Turkish blessing to buy Getir Food from Mubadala, sources say

items.description:
Uber Technologies announced Monday it has agreed to acquire the delivery operations of Turkish rapid-delivery startup Getir from Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund Mubadala Investment Company, marking the ride-hailing giant's latest push to expand its food delivery footprint in the Middle East.

The deal, pending regulatory approval, covers Getir's full delivery portfolio in Türkiye, including food, grocery, retail, and water delivery services. Under the terms, Uber will pay $335 million in cash to acquire 100 percent of Getir's food delivery business and invest an additional $100 million for a 15 percent stake in the grocery, retail, and water operations, with a complete acquisition of the remaining delivery portfolio expected over the coming years based on performance conditions.[1][2][3]

items.title: Scientists detect first underground lava tube on Venus

featured_image.name: Radar data reveals cavernous underground lava tube on Venus

items.description: Researchers at the University of Trento in Italy have identified the first subsurface feature ever detected on Venus: a massive lava tube beneath a shield volcano in the planet's northern hemisphere. The finding, published Monday in the journal Nature Communications, provides direct evidence of underground volcanic structures on Earth's neighboring planet, previously only theorized by scientists.[1][2]

items.title: China tells banks to cut US Treasury holdings, citing market risks

featured_image.name: China cuts US Treasury stockpile, dropping to No 3 spot ...

items.description: Chinese regulators have quietly advised domestic financial institutions to limit new purchases of US government bonds and begin reducing existing holdings, citing concerns over concentration risks and market volatility, according to Bloomberg. The directive, issued in recent weeks to major lenders, sent Treasury yields higher and the dollar lower as markets opened Monday.[1][2]

items.title: UN says 53 migrants dead or missing after boat sinks off Libya

featured_image.name: Dozens of migrants feared dead after boat capsizes off Libya ...

items.description:
A rubber dinghy carrying 55 migrants capsized off the coast of Libya early Friday, leaving at least 53 people dead or missing, the United Nations' International Organization for Migration reported Monday. Two babies were among those lost in what the agency described as "yet another deadly incident along the Central Mediterranean route."[1][2][3]

Only two survivors, both Nigerian women, were rescued by Libyan authorities following a search-and-rescue operation. One woman reported losing her husband, while the other said she lost her two children in the tragedy. IOM teams provided emergency medical care to the survivors upon their disembarkation.[2][4][1]

items.title: Starmer faces mounting calls to resign after top aides depart

featured_image.name: Morgan McSweeney resigns as chief of staff to UK Prime ...

items.description:
British Prime Minister Keir Starmer is fighting for his political survival after two senior Downing Street officials resigned within 24 hours and the Scottish Labour leader publicly called for him to step down.

Tim Allan, Starmer's director of communications, resigned on Monday, just one day after chief of staff Morgan McSweeney departed, plunging the government deeper into crisis over the appointment of Peter Mandelson as UK ambassador to the United States despite his ties to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.[1][2]

Scottish Labour leader Anas Sarwar became the most senior Labour politician to demand Starmer's resignation, declaring at a hastily arranged press conference in Glasgow: "The distraction needs to end and the leadership in Downing Street has to change". Sarwar warned that failures at the heart of Downing Street were jeopardizing Labour's chances in the May Scottish parliamentary elections.[3][4][5]

items.title: Discord to require face scans or IDs for full access in March

featured_image.name: Discord will require a face scan or ID for full access next ...

items.description:
Discord announced on Sunday that all users worldwide will be placed into a restricted "teen-by-default" experience starting in early March, requiring age verification through a face scan or government ID to unlock full platform access.

The gaming and chat platform, which has more than 200 million monthly active users, said the move is part of enhanced teen safety features timed to coincide with Safer Internet Day. Users who do not complete verification will face blurred sensitive content, blocked access to age-restricted channels and servers, and restricted direct message settings.[1][2]

items.title: Norwegian ambassador resigns over Epstein ties as scandal spreads

featured_image.name: Norwegian ambassador resigns as she faces scrutiny over contacts ...

items.description: The release of millions of Jeffrey Epstein documents by the U.S. Department of Justice on January 30 has sent shockwaves through political establishments across multiple continents, forcing resignations and triggering investigations from Norway to France to Slovakia, while the response in the United States remains comparatively muted.

items.title: China warns Japan of 'resolute response' after Takaichi landslide

featured_image.name: 2026-01-06t234827z_228273034_rc29gv9nytkl_rtrmadp_3_china-japan-exports-dual-use.jpg?itok=EX9_uK6T

items.description:
Beijing issued a sharp warning to Tokyo on Monday, urging Japan to retract Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's November remarks about potential military intervention over Taiwan, as China-Japan tensions escalate following her decisive election victory.

"If the far-right forces in Japan misjudge the situation and act recklessly, they will inevitably face resistance from the Japanese people and a resolute response from the international community," Foreign Ministry spokesman Lin Jian said at a regular news conference on February 9. He added that Japan must "demonstrate basic sincerity in safeguarding the political foundation of China-Japan relations through concrete actions."[1][2]

items.title: Kremlin says it's in talks to aid Cuba amid US 'suffocating' sanctions

featured_image.name: Russia will continue to supply oil to Cuba, RIA cites ambassador

items.description:
The Kremlin on Monday accused the United States of imposing "suffocating measures" on Cuba and pledged to continue discussions with Havana on providing energy assistance, even as the United Kingdom threatens military action against the Russian tankers that would deliver such aid.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters that "the situation is really critical in Cuba" and that Russia is "negotiating with our Cuban friends to find potential solutions to these issues, at least to give what help we can." The statement comes days after Russian Ambassador to Cuba Viktor Coronelli confirmed to state news agency RIA Novosti that Moscow's oil shipments to the island would persist despite Washington's warnings of tariffs on countries supplying fuel to the Caribbean nation.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: EU threatens emergency action to force Meta to reopen WhatsApp to AI rivals

featured_image.name: Meta warned EU plans to impose measures to reverse WhatsApp AI ...

items.description:
The European Commission issued a formal warning to Meta on Monday, threatening to impose emergency measures that would force the tech giant to allow rival artificial intelligence chatbots back onto WhatsApp while an antitrust investigation continues.

EU regulators delivered a "statement of objections" to Meta, setting out a preliminary finding that the company breached competition rules by blocking third-party AI assistants from accessing its messaging platform. The move escalates a probe launched in December 2025 following Meta's decision to ban general-purpose AI chatbots from WhatsApp's business tools.[1][2][3]
